about: Label a row of our timeline as fact, evidence or hypothesis by this site's rules. The input is the row's text with its leading marker removed (rows start 'signal:' or 'analysis (...)': that would give the answer away) and its source labels. The gold is the row's label in signals.json, which tools/timeline.mjs derives from the lead's markers. Rows that quote the press or point at a private person's post are left out.

input.text: AEMET, Spain's meteorological agency, says in public that the storm is named Charles, 2 h 57 min before the 13:17 this timeline gives for IPMA's communiqué no. 1 (row s-1109T1317). AEMET's post is timed 10:20:11 (read through Bluesky's public API). IPMA's communiqué no. 1 can no longer be read (its page and feed carry only no. 2), so whether 13:17 was its first publication or an edit is not established

IPMA names the storm CHARLES (communiqué no. 1): expected north of Madeira at 00:00 on 11 Nov, then toward the mainland, "com elevada incerteza na trajetória e intensidade"; orange warnings to be issued

Neither step is confirmed at Lusoponte, whose site has not answered our hourly tries; what holds on Wednesday under the red wind is not announced

input.text: the official and model data are consistent with the centre passing very close to Lisbon at about 17:00 to 18:00 Wednesday, more likely just south of it (met.no's pressure minimum 986.7 hPa at 17:00 to 18:00 and a 160° wind swing in an hour; the guidance has moved). Against: IPMA's red wind unchanged, its track text already includes Lisbon, no communiqué no. 3, point models move. It does not lower the danger: the worst moves toward the passage, about 16:00 to 19:00, and a lull near the centre is not the end. Wednesday tests it: wind backing east then north and pressure near 987 hPa means it passed south

input.text: The alert situation's legal text, read at source: Despacho n.º 13773-A/2026 (Diário da República n.º 218/2026, Suplemento, Série II, 10 November), by the Presidency of the Council of Ministers and nine ministries, under Lei 27/2006: in force 00:00 to 23:59 on 11 November, measures 2(a) to (e) and readiness measures 3(a) to (f). It suspends outdoor events (2(b)) and does not mention Web Summit: "formally advised" has no legal text; it remains the organisers' own wording (their page, 19:09) beside the government's recommendation reported at 17:53
sources: read 02:28 by incident.researcher@ (the site is a JavaScript app; read with a browser)

input.text: which side of Lisbon the centre passes is unsettled: "just south of Lisbon" drops to low confidence (was medium), because met.no's 01:19 run veers the wind through south to west with its strongest mean wind (56 to 58 km/h) at 14:00 to 15:00 and lowest pressure 987.7 hPa at 15:00, the pattern of a centre passing just north; IPMA's hourly model (an older run) and its forecasters on radio lean the other way. What holds across the inputs (medium confidence): the centre passes very close to Lisbon between about 15:00 and 18:00. The press headline "less wind for Lisbon" is not supported by these inputs. IPMA's red warnings for Lisbon stand; this is our analysis, not a forecast
sources: data/weather/analysis.md section 7b (7 and 7a kept, dated); met.no and IPMA figures in data/weather/forecast.json, read 01:19 and 02:22
